evals.name: check-reports-memory-root-and-writes-nothing
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check with no argument. Reports the memory root the verification skills resolve (.work/ unless the project's instructions declare another root) as INFO, probes a representative file path under it with git check-ignore -v, and writes nothing. It says there is nothing to configure because placement is fixed by the artifact protocol.
expectations: Treats no argument as check
Reports the memory root, or the root a project instruction declares, as INFO
Probes a representative file path rather than only the directory
Writes no file and runs no verification pass

evals.name: apply-does-not-configure-artifact-placement
evals.prompt:
/verification:setup apply

Persist my artifact directory settings.
evals.expected_output: Says artifact placement is not configurable: manifests, baselines and raw captures land in the memory slice <memory_dir>/<slug>/ and are never committed. The only settings apply writes are proof_level and live_workers in docs/conventions/verification.yaml, so with neither key named it writes nothing, creates no .claude/ concern file, and does not edit any ignore file.
expectations: States that artifact placement has nothing to persist
Names the memory slice as the placement and does not invent a configuration file
Does not write docs/conventions/verification.yaml when no proof level was asked for
Does not edit any ignore file or the consumer's root .gitignore

evals.name: absent-ignore-guard-is-info-not-fail
evals.prompt:
/verification:setup check

No verification run has happened in this repo yet, so .work/ does not exist.
evals.expected_output: Reports the ignore probe as INFO, not FAIL: the memory root's self-ignoring .gitignore is created by the first memory-slice write, so its absence before any run is expected. It does not create the directory or the guard file.
expectations: Reports the missing guard as INFO, never FAIL
Explains that the first memory-slice write creates the guard
Creates no directory and no .gitignore

evals.name: apply-changes-existing-file-only-after-diff-confirmed
evals.prompt:
/verification:setup apply proof_level=strict

The repository already has docs/conventions/verification.yaml with `proof_level: path`.
evals.expected_output: Runs setup-apply.mjs proof_level=strict, which exits 3 and prints a unified diff because the existing file would change. Shows the operator that diff and asks; re-runs with --yes only on an explicit yes. Before recommending strict it says members on an older verification release do not read the file. After the write it re-runs the check row and reports the value read back, notes that /verification:confirm reads the default branch copy so the level applies once merged, and reports whether the file is tracked.
expectations: Shows the diff and waits for an explicit yes before passing --yes
Reports the value the check reads back, not the value it wrote
Says the level takes effect once the file is merged to the default branch

evals.name: apply-refuses-unlisted-level
evals.expected_output: Refuses: thorough is not one of path, live, strict. The script prints one refusal line, exits 1 and writes nothing. The skill reports the allowed values and does not invent a new level or write a different file.
expectations: Refuses the value and names the allowed levels path, live and strict
Writes no file
Does not add a key or level the schema does not list

evals.name: apply-writes-live-workers
evals.prompt:
/verification:setup apply live_workers=3

The repository has no docs/conventions/verification.yaml yet.
evals.expected_output: Takes live_workers=3 from the argument without asking and runs setup-apply.mjs with that argument, which creates docs/conventions/verification.yaml holding live_workers: 3. It does not also write or ask for proof_level. It re-runs the check row and reports the live_workers value read back, notes that /verification:confirm reads the default branch copy, and reports whether the file is tracked.
expectations: Runs setup-apply.mjs with the argument live_workers=3
Does not ask for a value or write a proof_level key
Reports the live_workers value the check reads back and whether the file is tracked

evals.name: apply-refuses-zero-live-workers
evals.prompt:
/verification:setup apply live_workers=0

The repository already has docs/conventions/verification.yaml with `live_workers: 2`.
evals.expected_output: Runs setup-apply.mjs live_workers=0, which refuses with one line (0 is not a whole number of at least 1), exits 1 and writes nothing. The skill reports the refusal and that live_workers must be a whole number of at least 1, leaves the existing file with live_workers: 2, and does not substitute another value or pass --yes.
expectations: Reports that live_workers=0 was refused because it is not a whole number of at least 1
Leaves docs/conventions/verification.yaml unchanged, still live_workers: 2
Does not write a different value in place of 0
